task: If I'm 30, plan to retire at 65, and can save $300/month, with a 3% annual return, 13% current tax rate, and 24% retirement tax rate, show the comparison chart between Traditional and Roth IRA.
agent_final_answer:
I used the Chase / J.P. Morgan "IRA calculator" (Comparing Roth Vs. Traditional IRA), reachable from Chase.com search. I set the inputs to: Age range 30 to 65, Starting balance $0, Monthly contribution $300, Annual rate of return 3%, Current tax rate 13%, Estimated tax rate at retirement 24%.

The "Estimated account value" comparison chart was generated, comparing four account types over time (2026-2061). Final projected values at retirement (year 2061):

Account Type                      | Value at Retirement
----------------------------------|--------------------
Roth IRA                          | $224,000
General (taxable) account         | $207,000
Non-deductible Traditional IRA    | $201,000
Deductible Traditional IRA        | $197,000

Result: The Roth IRA produces the highest balance and beats both Traditional IRA options. This is because the assumed retirement tax rate (24%) is higher than the current tax rate (13%) - paying tax now (Roth) is better than deferring it (Traditional) when future tax rates are higher.
